title: mirror
body:
## mirror

Adds the reflection of a copy of the input mesh across the selected local axis planes with Blender's Mirror modifier; the planes pass through the input object's local origin, and merge welds vertices that land on the mirror plane (Blender's 0.001 merge distance). Use it to model one half or quarter of a symmetric part and complete it.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Primitives have their origin at centre, so mirroring a whole primitive overlaps it with itself; model only one side of the plane.
- To mirror about a world plane after transform, insert applyTransform so the local origin is the world origin.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `mirror`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axes` | Which local axes to mirror across, as [x, y, z] switches (Blender use_axis). [true, false, false] reflects across the YZ plane through the object origin; enabling several axes produces 2, 4 or 8 instances. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"boolean"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[true,false,false]` |
| `merge` | When true, vertices that end up within Blender's merge distance (0.001 local units) of their mirror image are welded, so a half-model with vertices on the mirror plane becomes one connected surface. Turn it off to keep the halves separate. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
